## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The containment check in `preview` compares paths as text without resolving them, so a relative path containing `..` still reads files outside home. The added test only checks an absolute outside path, so it misses this. `settings_file` and the 200-character truncation look correct and are tested.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))` compares the path text without resolving `..` or symlinks. For `preview("/home/u", "../../etc/passwd")`, `candidate` is `/home/u/../../etc/passwd`. That still starts with `/home/u`, so the check passes and line 14 reads `/etc/passwd`. A symlink inside home, such as `home/link -> /etc`, also gets through. Could you resolve both sides before comparing, e.g. `candidate = (Path(home) / relative).resolve()` and `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home).resolve())`? Please also add a `"../outside.txt"` case to `tests/test_paths.py:19-20`, which currently tests only an absolute path. — Anyone who controls `relative` can read any file the process can read, which defeats the "outside home" check.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — `candidate.read_text()[:200]` reads and decodes the whole file only to keep 200 characters. Previewing a multi-gigabyte log in home loads all of it into memory. Could you open the file and call `f.read(200)` instead? — Large files cause heavy memory use or a memory error just to show a short preview.
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — `read_text()` uses the default text encoding. Previewing a binary file in home, such as a `.png` or `.zip`, raises `UnicodeDecodeError` instead of returning a preview. Should this pass `errors="replace"`, or should binary files be rejected with a clear error? — Previewing any non-text file in home crashes with an unhandled decode error.

## Strengths
- `tests/test_paths.py:17-18` checks the truncation limit with a 500-character file and expects exactly 200 characters back.
- `settings_file` (`app/paths.py:17-18`) is a straightforward path join, and `tests/test_paths.py:23-26` checks its exact result.
